questions.question: For `attrs = '{"brand":"Acme"}'`, what is the difference between `attrs->'$.brand'` and `attrs->>'$.brand'`?
options: There is no difference; both are aliases of JSON_EXTRACT()
`->` returns text and `->>` returns a JSON array
`->` returns the JSON value "Acme" with quotes; `->>` also unquotes it to plain text Acme
questions.explanation: `->` is JSON_EXTRACT(); `->>` is JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT()), returning an unquoted string.

questions.question: Which statement about VIRTUAL and STORED generated columns in InnoDB is correct?
options: A VIRTUAL column is computed on read and can still have a secondary index, which materialises its values in the index
Only STORED columns can be indexed
VIRTUAL columns take more row space than STORED columns
A VIRTUAL column can be the PRIMARY KEY
questions.explanation: InnoDB supports secondary indexes on virtual columns; the values live in the index while the row stores nothing. Virtual columns cannot be the primary key.

questions.question: Which index type lets `WHERE '5g' MEMBER OF (attrs->'$.tags')` use an index on a JSON array?
options: A FULLTEXT index on the JSON column
A plain index created directly on the JSON column
A multi-valued index using `CAST(... AS ... ARRAY)`
questions.explanation: Multi-valued indexes (8.0.17+) store one entry per array element and serve MEMBER OF, JSON_CONTAINS and JSON_OVERLAPS. JSON columns cannot be indexed directly.

questions.question: When is storing data in a JSON column usually the wrong design?
options: When attributes are sparse and vary between rows
When a field is filtered, joined or must reference another table on most queries
When you mostly read the payload back whole
When the document is smaller than 1 KB
questions.explanation: Frequently queried or related fields belong in typed columns or child tables, which give foreign keys, strong typing and simple indexing.
